result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A defines three named lockups and gives each placement one clear choice with consistent, buildable proportions, so a volunteer could follow it without coming back with questions. B covers more ground, including a small-size silhouette fallback and stroke minimums for canvas. But it leaves the tote choice open ('pick one') and has confusing or wrong instructions: it says to fill gaps 'wider than' 1/16 in, keep the mark 'within' 2 in of the seam, and its dark-canvas note is unclear. A's weaker spot is the tote: it says little about how fine detail survives on canvas. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B names three lockups up front and assigns each placement clearly. It sets a concrete switch point (below 24 px, use the symbol only) and gives accurate tote positioning. A covers similar ground with more tote detail, but it has errors: it puts the mark within 2 in of the seam instead of clear of it, says to fill gaps wider than 1/16 in when narrow gaps are what close up, and mixes its x unit with cap height. A also never gives a minimum size for the full lockup.
